title: Spike: Incident tagging pipeline (incident-bot -> datastore -> dashboards) — notes
content:
Context / why this spike exists
- We need incident taxonomy fields to show up reliably in reporting (incident volume by category, MTTR/TTM by owner, by surface/region/tier).
- Source of truth for incident “facts” during response is Slack via incident-bot modals/commands.
- Metrics live in Prometheus + Grafana (and some SLO calculations in slo-toolkit). We need a join key + a small datastore so dashboards can slice incidents by taxonomy dimensions.
- This is NOT building a new IM product; goal is minimal, robust plumbing.

Goals (v0)
- Capture incident declaration + updates from incident-bot with standardized metadata fields (category, surface, service, owner team, region, tier, contributing factors, etc.).
- Persist to a queryable store with history (status changes + reclassifications).
- Join incident data with metrics/SLO dataset for:
  - incident counts by category/owner
  - MTTR by category/owner
  - error budget burn correlation by service/category
  - “time to categorize” / “time to assign owner” compliance

Non-goals
- Real-time incident timeline UX beyond what Slack already provides.
- A full incident graph / root-cause tracking.
- Complex semantic enrichment (LLM classification, etc.) in v1.

Assumptions / constraints
- Taxonomy values should be enforced (allowed values) at the time of declare/escalate (or within 15 minutes if we decide that policy).
- Must tolerate edits/reclassification post-incident (postmortem corrections).
- Must not break existing severity definitions or paging.
- Private incidents: included only where Redwood is the primary operator; security incidents remain under Security IR but may share metadata fields.

Current state (as of Jan 2025)
- incident-bot writes a channel + pinned message; some fields in the Slack message are free-text and inconsistent.
- SRE postmortems are in Confluence; partial structured fields exist but not consistently populated.
- Dashboards: manual tagging / ad-hoc spreadsheets for category analysis.

Proposed architecture (v0)
1) Source events
   - Slack incident-bot creates/updates incident via:
     - /incident declare modal submission
     - /incident update (status, severity changes)
     - ownership suggestion (based on selected category + service) (see incident-bot/pr_223)
   - Optional: control-plane emits “degraded mode” annotations (redwood/pr_10421) — can become contributing factor hints later.

2) Ingestion path
   - incident-bot posts structured payload to an internal webhook endpoint (owned by Observability or SRE tooling).
   - Endpoint validates:
     - required fields present (category, impacted_surface, service, severity, start_time, region, customer_tier)
     - values are in allow-list (synced from incident-metadata-standard)
     - incident_id is present and stable
   - On success: persist to datastore + emit audit log event.
   - On failure: incident-bot warns in Slack (actionable error) and optionally allows a short “unknown” placeholder for 10–15 minutes (policy decision).

3) Storage options (spike decision)
   A) Postgres (existing internal ops DB)
      - Pros: easy upserts + relational joins; easy history table; good for low-volume.
      - Cons: not great for wide analytics queries unless mirrored.

   B) ClickHouse (if already in use for telemetry)
      - Pros: analytics friendly, time series slicing fast.
      - Cons: operational overhead; schema evolution needs care.

   C) BigQuery/Snowflake (if we’re already landing other analytics here)
      - Pros: best for aggregated reporting; easy to share with BI.
      - Cons: latency (not truly real-time) and more infra if not already standardized.

   Recommendation for v0: Postgres as system-of-record + daily/hourly export to analytics (BigQuery or ClickHouse depending on existing pipeline). Keep Grafana querying the analytics store for dashboards.

Data model (proposed)
- Important: we need a stable incident identifier not dependent on Slack channel name.
- incident_id format suggestion: INC-YYYYMMDD-#### (generated by bot) or UUID with a display alias.

Tables / entities (conceptual — keep minimal)
1) incidents (current state)
   - incident_id (pk)
   - created_at
   - started_at (as declared)
   - resolved_at
   - severity (Sev0–Sev3 per existing policy)
   - status (declared | investigating | monitoring | resolved)
   - title
   - slack_channel_id
   - slack_message_ts (canonical message)
   - primary_owner_team (e.g., eng-platform, eng-infra, eng-runtime, eng-observability, eng-sre)
   - owning_service (controlled list where possible; allow “unknown” only temporarily)
   - incident_category (taxonomy v1)
   - impacted_surface (Hosted API | Dedicated | Private | Console | Control Plane | Edge/Gateway | Observability)
   - region (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-central-1, etc.)
   - customer_tier (free | self_serve | dedicated | enterprise) — align with Support/CS
   - customer_impact (none | degraded | partial_outage | full_outage)
   - comms_required (yes/no)

2) incident_events (append-only history)
   - incident_id
   - event_ts
   - event_type (declare | update | reclassify | assign_owner | resolve | reopen)
   - actor (slack_user_id)
   - payload_json (raw) — NOTE: if we do this in Postgres, keep it as text/jsonb but dashboards should rely on extracted columns.

3) incident_dimensions (optional; normalized lists)
   - This may be overkill for v0. For now keep allow-lists in code + in a config table with versioning.

Allowed values + versioning
- We need to ship allow-lists (category, contributing_factors, impacted_surface, services) with a version tag.
- Put a taxonomy_version field on incidents and events.
- When taxonomy values change:
  - ingestion continues accepting old values for a deprecation window
  - dashboards map old->new in a lookup table
  - postmortems can reclassify (event logged)

Joining incident metadata to metrics/SLO data
What we want on dashboards:
- Panel: “Incident count by category (last 30/90 days)”
- Panel: “MTTR by category + owner team”
- Panel: “Error budget burn vs incident category for service X”

Join keys (options)
1) service_name
   - Most direct, but our metrics labels are inconsistent (service, job, route, cluster) depending on component.
   - Requires a service label normalization table.

2) slo_id / slo_name (from slo-toolkit)
   - If incident-bot can select “impacted SLO” (optional field), join becomes trivial.
   - But adds cognitive load during declare. Probably optional field (postmortem/backfill can set).

3) control plane annotations / routing degraded events
   - Useful for correlation but not sufficient as primary join.

Suggested v0 approach
- Required: owning_service (from a curated list that matches SLO service naming) + impacted_surface.
- Optional: impacted_slo_ids (multi-select, can be empty during incident, filled after).
- Create a small “service_catalog” mapping:
  - incident_service_name -> metrics_service_label(s) -> slo_service_key
  - owner team + slack escalation channel (will come from the ownership-map sheet)

Data flow to dashboards
- Dashboards should query a denormalized view/table:
  incident_facts_daily or incident_facts (one row per incident with current classification)
  plus a second table for event history (for “time to categorize” / compliance).

Grafana + metrics overlay options
- Option A: Grafana uses mixed data sources (Prometheus for metrics + analytics store for incident facts).
  - Pros: easiest, no big data engineering.
  - Cons: cross-source joins are limited; overlay is mostly via annotations.

- Option B: replicate key metrics aggregates into analytics store (hourly rollups) so we can join in SQL.
  - Pros: true joins in SQL; easier “correlate incident to burn.”
  - Cons: more pipeline work; duplication of metric data.

Recommendation
- v0: Use Grafana annotations + side-by-side panels (incident counts + burn), with lightweight SQL for incident stats.
- v1: Add SLO rollup export from slo-toolkit to analytics store (already partially happening in slo-toolkit/pr_97).

Operational concerns / edge cases
- Reclassification: category/owner/service often wrong during declare; must allow update without losing original.
  - Store both current state and history.
  - For reporting, we should use “final_category” (last set before resolve or within X days).

- Multiple regions/surfaces: a single incident can impact multiple.
  - v0: single region + surface required, allow “multi” or “global” region value.
  - v1: support arrays (but our storage + dashboards get more complex). Given tooling constraint (no nested fields in some paths), keep v0 scalar with “global/multi”.

- Dedicated pools: need pool_id / customer_account_id sometimes.
  - v0: optional fields: dedicated_pool, account_id (string), customer_name (string).
  - Privacy: account_id is internal; no PII.

- Slack outages: if Slack is degraded, incident-bot ingestion fails.
  - Mitigation: bot writes to Slack as best-effort; ingestion endpoint retries; allow manual backfill via admin CLI.

- Backfill: last 90 days labeling (ENG-4826)
  - Need import script that can write incidents + events w/ “backfilled_by” and “backfill_ts”.

Security / compliance notes
- Incident metadata may mention customer names; discourage free-text fields that end up in analytics.
- Restrict access to incident datastore to Eng/SRE/Support leadership; dashboards aggregated for broader audiences.
- For security incidents: allow a flag security_related=true but details remain in Security IR tooling. Do not ingest sensitive details.

Implementation sketch (who does what)
- Devon Price: incident-bot emits structured payload on declare/update (behind feature flag).
- Mei Lin: backfill/import tooling + export job to analytics store (if needed).
- Logan Wright: ingestion endpoint + schema + dataset ownership; coordinate with SRE.
- Sergio Costa: Grafana dashboards using incident facts dataset.
- Allison Grant: ensure allowed values align with incident-metadata-standard and stay minimal.

Minimal API contract (incident-bot -> ingestion)
- POST /incident-events
  - headers: X-Redwood-Signature (HMAC) + timestamp
  - body: event_type, incident_id, event_ts, actor, fields (category, service, surface, severity, region, tier, etc.), taxonomy_version
- Response: 200 ok; 4xx validation w/ field errors

Rollout plan
1) Ship ingestion endpoint + Postgres tables in staging.
2) Enable incident-bot payload emit in staging (feature flag).
3) Dogfood with SRE on-call for 1 week; validate dashboards match manual labels.
4) Enable production for Sev0/Sev1 only first (so we catch validation pain early).
5) Expand to all severities; begin backfill.

Open questions (need decisions)
- Required-at-declare vs required-within-15-min: policy + bot UX. Current leaning: require category + surface + service at declare; allow “unknown” only with an auto-reminder.
- Do we require impacted_slo_ids? Probably NO (optional) due to cognitive load.
- Storage target for analytics: do we already have a standard (ClickHouse vs BigQuery)? I need final answer from Observability infra.
- Who owns the allow-lists + how are changes approved? Proposed: Allison (standards) + SRE sponsor sign-off; changes via PR.
- Naming: “owning_service” must match service catalog used by SLOs; need mapping doc from Platform/Infra.

Notes to self
- Make sure we can compute: time_to_owner_assigned, time_to_category_set, time_to_mitigate (TTM) once SLA mapping is in place.
- Keep payload minimal; do NOT dump whole Slack modal state into analytics.
- Don’t block incident declaration if Slack modal bug occurs; allow declare with minimal and require follow-up fields via /incident set-fields.
